title: Saving for something you love
description: A named goal, a picture, and a progress bar can make saving feel surprisingly good.

body.heading: Name it and price it
paragraphs: Saving 'for the future' is vague. Saving for 'the blue bike, about $180' is vivid. Write the goal, a realistic price, and a date you would love to reach it by.
Divide the price by the weeks until your date. That weekly number is your plan. If it is too big, extend the date or look for a good second-hand option — adjusting the plan is smart, not weak.

body.heading: Make progress visible
paragraphs: Draw a simple progress bar and colour it in as you save, or track it in an app. Visible progress is a quiet motivator, especially in the middle weeks when the goal feels far away.
Celebrate milestones cheaply: halfway there deserves a happy note to yourself, not a spending spree that undoes the work.

body.heading: Protect the goal
paragraphs: Keep goal money separate from daily spending if you can, even in a labelled envelope or sub-account. Money with a name is harder to spend by accident.

takeaway: Give your saving a name, a price, and a visible progress bar.
